chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Urwa, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:
Do not recite in the Prescribed Prayer anything from the determined Verses, for the prostration is an addition to the Prescribed Prayer.

key_terms.الْعَزَائِمِ: The determined Verses (specifically those requiring prostration)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on reciting the prostration verses (Ayat al-Sujah) during the obligatory prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic preference (or obligation, depending on the school of thought) against reciting the Ayat al-Sujah in the obligatory prayer to avoid the 'extra' prostration, preserving the prayer's structural integrity. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between the mandatory pillars of Salah and the recommended acts that, if performed, alter the prayer's count. The narration underscores the principle that adding un-prescribed physical acts, even if virtuous, can be legally significant in the context of the fixed ritual form.
